subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - SLOs & sizing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Wilson <tom.wilson@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - follow up & next steps

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on next steps and the validation scope: 

- SLO targets: P95 generation latency at <= 150ms (single-turn streaming), P99 <= 300ms.
- Throughput: baseline 2000 tokens/sec sustained, peak bursts up to ~6k tokens/sec.
- Concurrency: 80 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled (token-by-token).
- Model & infra interest: you mentioned wanting a comparison between NVIDIA A100 and H100 backends for both latency and cost-per-token.
- Data/traffic: you’ll share a sample traffic profile CSV and the formal SLO doc so we can size reserved throughput and propose a Dedicated config.

Proposed validation plan (high level):
1) We run a 2-day side-by-side validation: A100 vs H100, matching your traffic profile (payload distribution + streaming).
2) Measure P50/P95/P99 latency, end-to-end tail behavior with streaming, and token throughput at target concurrencies.
3) Report: recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec), GPU type, estimated committed capacity (vGPU/GPU count), and an expected cost delta.

Next steps from our side: Aditya (cc’d) will scope the validation run and share a proposed test matrix. From your side: please share the traffic profile + any special prompt/stop-token behavior you need us to emulate. If you prefer, we can sign an NDA/validation agreement before the runs — whatever you need.

Are you available for a 30-minute sync on Wed 3/3 to finalize the test matrix?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.com

Attachment: none in this message
From: Tom Wilson <tom.wilson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - follow up & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming the SLOs above (P95 <=150ms, P99 <=300ms) are what our product team will require for GA. A couple clarifying notes:

- Streaming behavior: we do token-by-token streaming for chat UI. Clients will open a connection and expect first-token latency impact to be minimal — i.e., cold-start behavior is important.
- Model flavor: we’re planning to evaluate a 2B-7B family first (custom-tuned), but we also want a baseline run on a 13B checkpoint to see scaling trends.
- Failure tolerances: we need graceful degradation — fallback to a cheaper model family if the primary cannot meet latency SLO for a brief window.

I’m attaching our traffic sample and SLO requirements doc (see attachments). We can do Wed 3/3 at 11:00 PT for a brief test-matrix sync — that works for me.

Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Attachments: MVP_traffic_profile.csv, SLO_requirements.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Wilson <tom.wilson@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - follow up & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the files, Tom.

Aditya / Dev / Neha: can you confirm the following so I can lock the test matrix before Wed?
- Test matrix: A100 vs H100, 2B/7B/13B checkpoints, streaming on, concurrency sweep at [10, 40, 80] sessions, bursts to 200% for 10-minute windows.
- Metrics to collect: P50/P95/P99 latency (first-token and full-response), throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, and end-to-end client-observed tail latency with simulated cold-cache scenarios.
- Validation window: 48 hours each config.

Also, I’ll generate a DocuSign for a basic validation agreement (standard mutual NDA + data handling notes) and send it to Tom prior to the run.

Tom — I’ll send calendar invite for Wed 3/3 11:00 PT. If you want us to include an SRE or product manager, let me know.

Cheers,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - test matrix & infra questions

Thanks — quick technical notes / requests from the validation engineering side: 

1) Can you confirm distribution of payload sizes (we saw the CSV but want to be explicit): what percent of requests are short (<64 tokens) vs medium (64-512) vs long (>512)? This matters for kernel selection and batching.
2) Do you have any enforced per-request timeouts or streaming window sizes? For instance, clients might cut a stream at 5s if no tokens are received.
3) For the A100/H100 comparison: do you have a cost preference (we can bias test configs to minimize cost or to maximize latency headroom).

Prelim plan: we’ll provision one H100 80GB and one A100 80GB equivalent cluster (matched as closely as possible) and run the traffic replay. For 13B checkpoints we may need 2x the GPU count to hit the concurrency targets; we’ll detail exact sizing in the test matrix doc we share before Wed.

Tom — if you can share the short/medium/long percentages and any client-side timeouts by EOD, we’ll finalize the matrix.

-Aditya
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Aditya / team —

Thanks. Quick answers:
- Payload distribution (from MVP_traffic_profile.csv): short ~55%, medium ~35%, long ~10%.
- Client timeouts: UI clients cut streams at 8s; server-to-server calls wait up to 30s. Please emulate both patterns.
- Cost preference: prioritize meeting P95/P99 SLOs, but also include a cost-per-token table in the final report.

We’re good to go for Wed 11:00 PT. I’ve attached the two files (sent earlier) and dropped a few example prompts in the CSV. We’ll be available during the test window for quick troubleshooting.

Tom
